% carrying the label, e.g. \subsection{Transfer figure: details}\label{app:exp3-main-details}
The original network in Figure~\ref{fig:exp3-main} was trained on DDM, RDM and CDM only. Zero-shot, the LBA is run under the RDM's model embedding, whose parameters ($v$, $v_{\mathrm{diff}}$, $a$, $\tau$, $s_v$, $s_\tau$, $\pi$) it shares, with the LBA's start-point range fixed at $A = 0.5$ so that $a$ is the mean distance an accumulator travels to its threshold, the quantity the RDM's $a$ measures. Fine-tuning continues training for 1000 epochs on all four families, drawn with equal probability, with the LBA under its own model embedding initialised from the RDM's. In the \emph{interaction} design, $v$, $v_{\mathrm{diff}}$, $a$, $\tau$ and $s_v$ carry slopes on $u_1$; $v$, $v_{\mathrm{diff}}$, $a$ and $\tau$ carry slopes on $u_2$; $v$, $v_{\mathrm{diff}}$ and $a$ on the product $u_1 u_2$ (18 coefficients in all). Both networks are evaluated on the same 200 benchmark test datasets (500 trials, two stimulus-coded alternatives) with 200 posterior draws per dataset, and each cell in panel A draws both on one frame; $\pi$ is estimated but not shown. NRMSE and calibration error are defined as in the bottom panel of Figure~\ref{fig:app1-ddm-intercept-only-cf}. With fine-tuning, the LBA's median NRMSE over coefficients falls from 0.159 to 0.105 (18 of 18 coefficients improve) and its median calibration error from 0.190 to 0.017 (16 of 18). The trained families' metrics barely move, but their posteriors do: classifier two-sample tests per dataset, against the draw-split null floor, give a median excess of $+0.020$ to $+0.048$ on this design, with 16--27\% of datasets above 0.10 (Table~\ref{tab:app3-forgetting-c2st}); on the intercept-only design the excess is $-0.065$ to $-0.040$, i.e.\ indistinguishable. The two arms' separate diagnostics for this design are in Figures~\ref{fig:app3-zeroshot-lba-interaction} and~\ref{fig:app3-finetuned-lba-interaction}; the metric changes for the other designs in Figures~\ref{fig:app3-delta-metrics-intercept-only}--\ref{fig:app3-delta-metrics-fixed-regressed}. Panel C uses the fine-tuned network's empirical lexical-decision fit with $s_v$ and $s_\tau$ estimated (the free-variability variant), fitted per subject with an intercept and the speed/accuracy condition on $v$, $v_{\mathrm{diff}}$, $a$ and $\tau$. Each posterior predictive draw simulates the subjects' own trials with contamination included and pools simulated trials across subjects and correct/error responses. The 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 quantiles are computed per draw, and the bands are their central 95\% intervals across draws. Word frequency is not part of the fitted design; lexicality enters through the favoured accumulator with a shared drift advantage for words and nonwords. The fitted model therefore does not represent frequency or lexicality effects beyond stimulus coding.
